![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14198769/assets/a84a2fa07d06dce3026740be2831127fd4d7f2d72fd31388df646ad7ac62e4ff.png)

The scatter plot for a sample of paired observations is shown above. What vectors correspond to the direction of the second principal component of the data?
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the *first principal component* of the data corresponds to the direction in which the data varies the most (the direction where we have the maximum variance).

The *second principal component* of the data corresponds to the direction perpendicular to the first principal component in which the data varies the most.

In our diagram, the direction where the variance changes the most corresponds (approximately) to the vector $a$ or to the vector $c,$ as shown below. So, $a$ or $c$ define the direction of the first principal component. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14198769/assets/4d025f8b6447b7a17e4c5fcfb192dcaf4c2bb1ea3a926961d25e94832972bee1.png)

  

Next, notice that in the 2D case, we have only one direction perpendicular to the first principal component. And this direction corresponds to the vector $b,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14198769/assets/e8d223a9a8a29f297a88f7d7c98d99776540e0ba0e0f3935892a356e92a8aac9.png)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is "$b$ only."
